terms.comment: Of binding, holding and packing close: artē conligāre, to tie tight; artius conlocāre, to set closer together (Sallust). Of affection, artē dīligere, to love dearly (Pliny); of sleep, “soundly”: artē dormīre (Cic. Div. 1.59). All from Lewis & Short.

terms.gloss: very close, next to; quam proximē, as close as possible
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.14.3: proximē Pompejum sedēbam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 6.5.3: exercitum habēre quam proximē hostem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of place, “right next to, closest to”, with the accusative or dative; with quam, “as close as possible”. Of time it means “most recently, last” (Lewis & Short).
Of people who live on close terms, conjūnctē vīvere (Nepos; Lewis & Short). In Cicero it is also “jointly, together with”.

phrases.english: I was sitting right next to Pompey
to keep the army as close to the enemy as possible

sources: Lewis & Short: artus · Lewis & Short: arte · Lewis & Short: propior · Lewis & Short: proxime · Lewis & Short: conjungo
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
